topic_groups.topic: Health Care Access, Workforce, Policy, and Ethics

articles.title: U.S. poll reveals many young adults may not be ready to manage their own health care
articles.summary_3_sentences: A national poll suggests many U.S. young adults may lack practical skills for managing their own health care. Nearly one in six parents reported that their 18- to 25-year-old child does not independently handle basic tasks such as scheduling appointments or providing family history.

articles.title: Emergency physician burnout: 1 in 10 leaving specialty in Canada
articles.summary_3_sentences: A CMAJ study reports that burnout is leading some emergency physicians in Canada to leave the specialty or reduce clinical hours. The findings add to concerns about workforce strain and emergency care capacity.

articles.title: Testosterone and combat readiness: What does the evidence really show?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article examines a U.S. defense proposal to measure testosterone levels in soldiers and offer treatment to those with low levels. It focuses on what evidence can and cannot show about testosterone, health, and military performance.

articles.title: Chinese university investigating girl's death in gene-editing trial
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Chinese university is investigating reports that a gene-editing trial caused the death of a 6-year-old girl. The report states that the death was not disclosed in the published research, raising concerns about trial oversight and transparency.

articles.title: Colorado was the first state to cap a drug's price. Then a federal court stepped in
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses Colorado's drug price review board, which has authority to set upper payment limits for certain high-cost medicines. A federal court intervention has affected the state's first attempt to cap a drug price.

articles.title: US panel endorses more unproven if buzzy peptides
articles.summary_3_sentences: A U.S. review panel recommended loosening restrictions on most of a group of popular peptides. Medical experts cited in the article objected that the products are not sufficiently studied to justify broader access.

articles.title: US court rules abortion pill restrictions 'unlawful'
articles.summary_3_sentences: A federal court in Virginia ruled that restrictions imposed by the U.S. drug regulator on mifepristone were unlawful. The court ordered the Trump administration to reconsider the restrictions.

articles.title: FDA-issued sodium targets yield no apparent impact
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that the FDA's 2021 voluntary sodium reduction targets appear to have had minimal impact on new packaged foods. Researchers compared sodium content in products introduced before and after the guidance.

articles.title: The billion-dollar problem keeping Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound from patients
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that GLP-1 drugs such as Ozempic, Wegovy, and Zepbound may provide strong health value but could strain insurance budgets if widely covered. The article also notes concerns about low-cost compounded versions and the need for long-term treatment support.

topic_groups.topic: Cancer Biology, Immunotherapy, and Oncology Tools

articles.title: Bile Acid Drives Cancer Progression (Popular)
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers examined how bile acid activity may contribute to cancer progression. The report links bile acid to tumor growth and aggressive cancer behavior, suggesting it may be explored as a therapeutic target.

articles.title: Novel Antibody Effectively Targets Prostate Cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A novel antibody was tested for its ability to recognize prostate cancer cells. Laboratory and experimental model results reportedly showed strong target binding and reduced tumor growth, indicating preclinical therapeutic potential.

articles.title: AI analyzes surgical technique to improve prostate cancer care
articles.summary_3_sentences: Cedars-Sinai investigators reported that AI analysis of surgeons' movements during procedures may help predict patient recovery. The findings, published in npj Digital Medicine, suggest surgical gesture analysis could help refine prostate cancer surgical care.

articles.title: CRISPR makes prostate cancer vulnerable to immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists used CRISPR to alter prostate cancer cells so the immune system could detect and attack them more effectively. The experimental approach improved immunotherapy effects in mice, so the findings remain preclinical.

articles.title: Aggressive Bladder Cancer Outcomes Improve with Addition of Immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports improved outcomes in aggressive muscle-invasive bladder cancer when immunotherapy is added to treatment. Details in the provided record are limited, but the focus is on addressing a difficult clinical cancer subtype.

articles.title: Autoantibodies could shape cancer risk, growth and response to immunotherapy
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Cell commentary suggests that autoantibodies may influence cancer risk, tumor growth, and response to immunotherapy. The article frames autoantibodies as a possible explanation for why cancer develops or behaves differently among people with varying apparent risk.

articles.title: 'Pro version' of cisplatin keeps its cancer-killing power while reducing side effects
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers describe a modified version of cisplatin intended to preserve anticancer activity while reducing harm to healthy organs. The article highlights cisplatin's kidney and nerve toxicities as major reasons doses may need to be reduced or stopped.

articles.title: Novel Proteins Regulate Immune Cell Exhaustion
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers identified proteins that regulate immune cell exhaustion during chronic infection. The report suggests that modulating these proteins may restore aspects of T-cell activity and inform future immunotherapy approaches.

topic_groups.topic: Nutrition, Metabolism, Gut Health, and Weight Management

articles.title: Artificial Sweeteners May Impair the Growth of Gut Microbes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Research examined how artificial sweeteners affect gut microbiota. The report says sweetener exposure impaired growth of beneficial microbes and reduced microbial diversity in experiments, suggesting possible gut-health effects.

articles.title: A tax on sugary drinks in Egypt could reduce disease and save US$1.8 billion in health care costs: Modeling study
articles.summary_3_sentences: A modeling study estimates that a sugary drink tax in Egypt could reduce noncommunicable disease and save health care costs. The study focuses on diet-related conditions such as heart disease, stroke, diabetes, and cancer.

articles.title: Could sparkling water be a better choice for your teeth?
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study comparing beverage effects on mouth acidity suggests unsweetened sparkling water may be less harmful for teeth than sugar-sweetened soda. The article focuses on dental acidity rather than broader nutritional outcomes.

articles.title: Why losing the wrong fat can trigger diabetes
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists report that damaged fat cells can become inflamed, lose lipid-storage capacity, and disappear. The findings suggest diabetes risk may arise not only from excess fat but also from loss of healthy fat tissue needed for metabolic regulation.

articles.title: Time-restricted eating may help retain cognitive function in older adults
articles.summary_3_sentences: A small pilot clinical trial in older women with overweight or obesity found modest cognitive improvements with time-restricted eating during a weight-loss program. The results are preliminary and compare limiting the daily eating window with calorie reduction alone.

articles.title: Your AI calorie-tracking app may be off by 345 calories
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of AI-powered food apps found that four apps underestimated calories and fat by about one-third compared with carefully prepared meals. High-fat ketogenic dishes appeared especially difficult for the apps, while carbohydrate estimates were more consistent.

articles.title: Photo-based calorie-tracking apps may underestimate energy in meals
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found that four photo-based calorie-tracking apps underestimated meal calories and fat content by about one-third. The article notes that these AI tools are convenient but may miss a substantial portion of meal energy.

articles.title: Teens who start the day with breakfast eat better overall, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study of teens around age 18 found that eating breakfast was linked with better overall nutrient intake. Breakfast consumption increased intake of fiber, iron, zinc, and choline among teens who tended to skip it.

articles.title: Prebiotic sodas typically contain as much sugar as fiber, raising questions about gut-health claims
articles.summary_3_sentences: An analysis of prebiotic sodas found that many contain relatively little prebiotic fiber and more sugar than consumers might expect from marketing claims. The article raises questions about how strongly these products can support gut-health claims.

articles.title: Plant-forward planetary health diet linked to lower heart disease risk
articles.summary_3_sentences: A 20-year study of more than 65,000 postmenopausal women found that higher adherence to the Planetary Health Diet was associated with lower cardiovascular disease risk. Outcomes included overall cardiovascular disease, coronary heart disease, stroke, and heart failure.

articles.title: A daily fiber supplement reduced knee arthritis pain and improved strength
articles.summary_3_sentences: A six-week trial found that a prebiotic fiber supplement reduced knee osteoarthritis pain and improved grip strength and pain sensitivity. The results point to a possible gut-muscle-pain connection, but the record does not provide details on trial size or durability.

articles.title: Oral GLP-1 drugs may quiet the brain's food craving circuit
articles.summary_3_sentences: Newer oral GLP-1-related drugs reduced pleasure-driven eating in mice by quieting a deep brain reward circuit. The finding is preclinical and may help researchers understand food cravings and related reward pathways.

articles.title: GLP-1 Drugs Could Help Slow Some Aging Processes
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that GLP-1 agonists, originally used for diabetes and weight loss, may influence some biological processes linked to aging. The report focuses on possible mechanisms and should not be read as proof that these drugs broadly slow aging in people.

articles.title: Intermittent Fasting Keeps Weight Off for a Year
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that participants practicing intermittent fasting maintained weight loss for one year. It also notes associations with improved heart-health markers, presenting fasting as a potential lifestyle approach for weight management.

articles.title: Coffee may help shield the liver from fat, scarring, and cancer
articles.summary_3_sentences: A long-term study linked coffee consumption with lower risks of cirrhosis, liver cancer, and death from liver disease. Coffee drinkers also had healthier liver scans and blood protein patterns, with benefits reported even at one or two cups daily.

articles.title: AI helps Stanford scientists discover "natural Ozempic" without the usual side effects
articles.summary_3_sentences: Stanford Medicine researchers identified a naturally occurring molecule, BRP, that may suppress appetite and reduce body weight. The article says BRP acts on a targeted brain region involved in hunger and metabolism, but the provided record does not establish clinical effectiveness in humans.

topic_groups.topic: Infectious Disease, Antivirals, and Antimicrobial Resistance

articles.title: A Novel Pathway Boosts COVID-19 & Drives Lung Damage
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a pathway that may increase COVID-19 infection and lung damage. Experimental data linked the pathway to increased viral replication in lung tissue and respiratory injury, suggesting a potential therapeutic target.

articles.title: A Working Antibacterial Resistance Gene is Found in Nature
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study found a functional antibacterial resistance gene in natural environments. The gene conferred resistance in bacterial assays, underscoring concerns about environmental reservoirs of resistance.

articles.title: Early respiratory infections may explain half of younger siblings' earnings gap
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports research linking early respiratory infections with part of the education and earnings gap observed between younger and older siblings. The finding suggests childhood infection exposure may contribute to long-term socioeconomic differences, though the summary does not establish individual causality.

articles.title: Will cough lozenges, syrups or medicated hot drinks make my cough go away?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reviews common over-the-counter approaches to cough relief, including lozenges, syrups, and medicated hot drinks. It focuses on what may help when a cough disrupts sleep or daily comfort.

articles.title: Dealing with post-pandemic sleep issues--it's not too late
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses persistent sleep disruption and anxiety after the COVID-19 pandemic, including in people with post-COVID-19 syndrome. It notes that these issues may contribute to ongoing fatigue.

articles.title: A new antiviral could stop measles before an outbreak takes off
articles.summary_3_sentences: An experimental pill prevented a measles-like virus from spreading through the air or close contact in ferrets. The drug worked around the time of exposure and shortened illness and contagiousness, but the findings are preclinical and would complement rather than replace vaccination.

topic_groups.topic: Neuroscience, Mental Health, Cognition, and Development

articles.title: Working memory rapidly updates its priorities after distractions, study finds
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study examined how working memory adjusts priorities after distractions. The article frames working memory as a core brain function for everyday tasks such as driving, chores, and work assignments.

articles.title: Premature babies who do not catch up well on growth may suffer brain abnormalities
articles.summary_3_sentences: A University of Granada study analyzed long-term consequences of extrauterine growth restriction in premature infants. Researchers identified possible persistent structural brain abnormalities among premature children who did not catch up well in growth.

articles.title: PTSD therapy walks patients through past trauma
articles.summary_3_sentences: University of Alberta researchers report evidence for a PTSD psychotherapy that combines confronting distressing memories with walking on a treadmill. The approach is presented as promising for recovery, based on the provided article summary.

articles.title: A hidden Alzheimer's tipping point may decide who gets dementia
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a possible tipping point that may influence whether Alzheimer's-related brain changes progress to dementia. The report points to immune-cell responses to plaques and tau as a potential target for extending cognitive resilience.

articles.title: Teens who struggle to log off social media could face increased ADHD symptoms over time
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article reports that teens who have difficulty disengaging from social media may face increased ADHD symptoms over time. It places the finding in the context of algorithm-driven platforms designed to keep users engaged.

articles.title: A single dose reversed autism-like symptoms in adult mice within hours
articles.summary_3_sentences: In a mouse model, mild inflammation during pregnancy was linked to adult offspring showing brain overactivity, sensory sensitivity, repetitive behaviors, and increased seizure risk. A single dose of rapamycin temporarily improved many symptoms within about two hours, but the results are preclinical and in mice.

articles.title: Superagers keep youthful memories but their DNA does not explain why
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers found that SuperAgers with unusually strong memory did not simply have fewer Alzheimer's-related genetic risks than typical older adults. The article suggests their resilience may involve still-unknown brain, body, lifestyle, or environmental factors.

articles.title: APOE2 may protect the brain from Alzheimer's and aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: The APOE2 gene, associated with longevity, may help protect brain cells by reducing DNA damage and aiding neuronal recovery from stress. The finding could guide research into therapies that mimic APOE2-related protective mechanisms.

topic_groups.topic: Clinical Practice, Medical Imaging, and Digital Health

articles.title: Leadership helps reduce stress in operating rooms
articles.summary_3_sentences: A Leiden study suggests that surgeons' leadership skills under pressure play an important role in operating room performance. The article emphasizes that effective performance under pressure begins before the operation itself.

articles.title: Smarter sonograms: Researcher uses generative AI to advance medical imaging
articles.summary_3_sentences: A researcher is using generative AI to improve the diagnostic clarity of sonograms. The article notes that ultrasound is noninvasive but often produces grainy images that can limit interpretation.

articles.title: Can Virtual Humans Transform Drug Discovery?
articles.summary_3_sentences: Deep Origin is developing virtual human models intended to improve drug discovery through in-silico testing. The platform aims to simulate physiology and disease pathways to identify experiments that may fail before costly laboratory or clinical work.

topic_groups.topic: Child, Family, Skin, Sleep, and Consumer Health

articles.title: Kids do feel the cold, so why won't they wear a sweater?
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article discusses why children may resist wearing sweaters even when adults think they are cold. It considers whether children experience cold differently, are asserting independence, and when caregivers should insist.

articles.title: The next skincare revolution could start with your immune system
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article explores the idea that future skincare may focus more directly on immune-system functions in the skin. It contrasts this with traditional skincare goals such as moisture retention, barrier support, sun protection, and anti-aging effects.

articles.title: Jetting off for a summer vacation? How to eat and drink to minimize jet lag
articles.summary_3_sentences: The article offers guidance on eating and drinking strategies intended to reduce jet lag during summer travel. The provided summary is brief, but the focus is on practical travel health measures.

articles.title: Cannabis Curbs Opioid Withdrawal & Cuts Use in Half
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study published in the Journal of Cannabis Research is reported to find reductions in opioid withdrawal severity with cannabis use. The article says opioid use was cut by about half, suggesting cannabis may be studied as an adjunct in opioid addiction treatment.

topic_groups.topic: Basic Biology, Evolution, Environmental Science, and Space Health

articles.title: Hidden genetic diversity helped inbred brown tree snakes conquer guam
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers used long-read DNA sequencing to uncover more than 19,000 large genetic differences in invasive brown tree snakes on Guam. Many variants were concentrated in genes related to immunity and smell, which may have helped the population survive inbreeding and spread.

articles.title: Inside the Backrooms: The internet's creepiest place is becoming a tourist attraction
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers describe how the fictional online world known as the Backrooms has evolved into a form of digital tourism. The article frames its popularity as an example of audiences emotionally entering and collaboratively building imaginary places online.

articles.title: Scientists trace the shocking origin of human eyes to an ancient "cyclops"
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers propose that a tiny one-eyed ancestor from nearly 600 million years ago influenced the evolution of vertebrate eyes. They also link its ancient median eye to the modern pineal gland, which helps synchronize sleep with daylight.

articles.title: Scientists discover a compound that could supercharge aging muscle repair
articles.summary_3_sentences: Scientists identified a sulfur-based compound called LASSS that appears to protect and enhance a protein involved in muscle repair. The discovery could inform future approaches to age-related muscle loss, but the provided record does not establish clinical use.

articles.title: Gene Therapy Improves Stem Cell Transplant Success
articles.summary_3_sentences: Researchers report that gene therapy techniques improved stem cell transplant outcomes. The work combined gene editing with transplantation and was associated with increased engraftment and fewer complications in the described study.

articles.title: Spaceflight Linked to Accelerated Aging
articles.summary_3_sentences: A study links long-term spaceflight with biological markers of accelerated aging in astronauts. The findings raise health questions for extended missions, though the provided record does not specify the study size or markers analyzed.
